claims.text: Which Places Spend the Most on Education?
claims.support: Which Places Spend the Most on Education?

claims.text: A cinematic tour of global public spending on education operating costs, based on World Bank data.
claims.support: A cinematic tour of global public spending on education operating costs, based on World Bank data.

claims.text: Cuba puts 13% of its national income into education. Japan spends just 2.6%.
In Africa, Botswana commits 9.5% of its income to schooling, and Namibia spends 8.9%.
This indicator counts current operating expenditures in education like wages, excluding capital investments.
claims.support: Education expenditure refers to the current operating expenditures in education, including wages and salaries and excluding capital investments in buildings and equipment.

claims.text: The USA spends 4.4% of its national income on schools.
Higher spenders include New Zealand at 7.4%, Saudi Arabia at 7.2%, Sweden at 7.1%, and Costa Rica at 6.9%.

claims.text: Near the bottom, Nigeria dedicates 0.8% of its national income to classrooms.
